THE PARLIAMENTARY DEBATES
OFFICIAL REPORT
IN THE TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY-THIRD SESSION OF THE RAJYA SABHA
Commencing on the 17th July, 2017/26th Ashadha, 1939 (Saka)

RAJYA SABHA
Monday, the 17th July, 2017/26th Ashadha, 1939 (Saka)
The House met at eleven of the clock,  
MR. CHAIRMAN  in the Chair.
(The National Anthem,  "Jana Gana Mana" was played.)
OBITUARY REFERENCES
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing 
away of Dr. Akhilesh Das Gupta , former Member of this House; Shri Anil Madhav 
Dave, sitting Member; Shri P. N. Sukul, Dr. Dasari Narayana Rao  and Shri Era 
Sezhiyan, former Members; Shri Palvai Govardhan Reddy , sitting Member; and 
Dr. C. Narayana Reddy  and Shri U. K . Lakshmana Gowda , former Members 
of this House.
Dr. Akhilesh Das Gupta  passed away on the 12th of April 2017 at the age 
of 56 years.
Born in March 1961, at Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, Dr. Gupta was educated at 
the Allahabad, Lucknow and Agra Universities. An educationist, a businessman and a 
sports administrator, he was associated with several educational institutions and made 
significant contribution in the field of higher education. He was the Chancellor of the 
Babu Banarasi Das University. He was also the Publisher and the Chief Editor of a 
few dailies in Lucknow. He was a badminton player of international level and he served 
as the President of the Badminton Association of India and the Olympic Association.
Dr. Gupta  served as Mayor of Lucknow from 1993 to 1995.
Dr. Akhilesh Das Gupta  represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House 
for three terms – from November, 1996 to November, 2002; from November, 2002 
to May, 2008; and again from November, 2008 to November, 2014. He served as 
Minister of State in the Ministry of Steel in the Union Council of Ministers from 
2006 to 2008. He was also the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary 
Standing Committee on Industry.
In the passing away of Dr. Akhilesh Das Gupta,  the country has lost a 
distinguished parliamentarian, an able administrator and a sports enthusiast.
Shri Anil Madhav Dave , Minister of State in the Union Council of Ministers 
and a sitting Member of this House, passed away on the 18th of May, 2017 at the 

2 Obituary [RAJYA SABHA] References
age of 60 years. Born in July, 1956, at Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh, Shri Dave  was 
educated at the Gujarati College, Indore.
A social worker, Shri Dave  worked assiduously for the conservation of river 
Narmada and its catchment area through Narmada Samagra , an organisation 
founded by him for the conservation of rivers and for addressing climate change 
and environmental issues. He was the founder and Vice-President of Jan Abhiyan 
Parishad, an organisation to interlink and empower Self-Help Groups and NGOs.
Shri Dave  was a prolific writer with several publications on various subjects 
and areas to his credit.
Shri Anil Madhav Dave  represented the State of Madhya Pradesh in this 
House for three terms from August, 2009 to June, 2010, from June, 2010 to June, 
2016 and again from June, 2016 till his sad demise. He was the Chairman of the 
Select Committees of the Rajya Sabha on (i) Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Bill, 
2015, (ii) Real Estate Regulation and Development Bill, 2013, and (iii) Prevention 
of Corruption (Amendment) Bill, 2013. He served as Minister of State (Independent 
Charge) of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in the Union 
Council of Ministers since July, 2016.
In the passing away of Shri Anil Madhav Dave , the country has lost a champion 
of environment protection, a distinguished parliamentarian and an able administrator.
Shri P. N. Sukul  passed away on the 28th of May, 2017, at the age of 85 years.
Born in February, 1932, at Faizabad in Uttar Pradesh, Shri Sukul was educated 
at the D.A.V . College, Kanpur.
A civil servant, Shri Sukul  served in the Uttar Pradesh Government Secretariat 
and was actively associated with several employees and labour welfare associations 
and organisations. He was the Founder General Secretary of the Mazdoor Parishad, 
Uttar Pradesh and Chairman of the All India State Government Employees Federation.
Shri Sukul  has several poems, short stories and essays in Hindi to his credit. 
He was the Editor of the Hindi fortnightly ' Karmaketu'. He was also an avid sports 
enthusiast. 
Shri P. N. Sukul  represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House for two 
consecutive terms — from July, 1980 to April, 1984 and again from April, 1984 to 
April, 1990. He served as the Chairman of the Committee on Petitions, Rajya Sabha 
from 1984 to 1986 and of the Joint Committees of Parliament on the Veterinary 
Council Bill, 1981 and the Indian Medical Council (Amendment) Bill, 1987.
In the passing away of Shri P. N. Sukul , the country has lost an able 
parliamentarian and a dedicated labour leader.

Obituary [31 January, 2017]   References 3
Dr. Dasari Narayana Rao  passed away on the 30th of May, 2017, at the age 
of 70 years.
Born in May, 1947, in West Godavari District of Andhra Pradesh, Dr. Rao 
contributed immensely to Telugu and Hindi Cinema as director, producer, dialogue-
writer, lyricist and actor. He championed the cause of women, girl child and the 
downtrodden by raising issues such as eradication of dowry, bonded labour and other 
social evils through his films. He also founded a school for the poor at Chennai 
and a Women's College at Palakole in Andhra Pradesh. Dr. Rao  was the founder 
publisher and editor of 'Udayam', a Telugu daily.
Dr. Rao  was awarded the Honorary Doctorate ' Kalaprapoorna' by the Andhra 
University for his contribution to Telugu cinema and culture. He was the President 
of the South Indian Film Chamber of Commerce and the Chairman of the Andhra 
Pradesh Film Industry Development Committee.
Dr. Dasari Narayana Rao  represented the State of Andhra Pradesh in this 
House for two consecutive terms - from April, 2000 to April, 2006 and from April, 
2006 to April, 2012. He served as the Minister of State in the Ministry of Coal and 
Ministry of Mines in the Union Council of Ministers from May, 2004 to April, 2008.
In the passing away of Dr. Dasari Narayana Rao , the country has lost a well-
known film personality, a distinguished parliamentarian and a dedicated social worker.
Shri Era Sezhiyan  passed away on the 6th of June, 2017, at the age of 94 years. 
Born in April, 1923, in Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu, Shri Sezhiyan  was 
educated at Annamalai University.
Shri Sezhiyan  started his career as a journalist and was Editor of Tamil dailies, 
'Nam Nadu', 'Manram' and 'Makkal Arasu'. He served as the President of South Zone 
Insurance Employees' Federation and was a Member of the National Integration Council 
and Indian Council of World Affairs. He has several books of short stories, one-act 
plays, dramas and articles on political, economic and social subjects to his credit.
Shri Sezhiyan  started his legislative career as a Member of the Third Lok Sabha 
in 1962. He was also a Member of the Fourth and Fifth Lok Sabha. He served as 
the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee from 1971 to 1973.
Shri Era Sezhiyan represented the State of Tamil Nadu in this House from 
April, 1978 to April, 1984. He also served as Chairman of the Committee on Papers 
Laid on the Table from 1982 to 1984.
In the passing away of Shri Era Sezhiyan , the country has lost a noted journalist, 
a distinguished parliamentarian and a political thinker.

4 Obituary [RAJYA SABHA] References
Shri Palvai Govardhan Reddy  passed away on the 9th of June, 2017, at the 
age of 79 years.
Born in November, 1936, at Mahabubnagar District of Telangana, Shri Reddy  
was educated at the Vivekavardhini College, Osmania University.
An agriculturist and social worker, Shri Reddy worked assiduously for the welfare 
of the farmers. He was a Member of the Managing Committee of the Andhra Pradesh 
Agricultural University. He served as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Forest 
Development Corporation Limited. He also served as Director of various Corporations.
Shri Reddy  started his legislative career as a Member of the Andhra Pradesh 
Legislative Assembly and was a Member of that Assembly for five terms, from 1967 
to 1972, 1972 to 1978, 1978 to 1983, 1983 to 1985 and again from 1999 to 2004. 
He was also a Member of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council from 2007 to 
2009. He served as Minister of State for Rural Water Supply, Youth Service and 
Leather Industries Development Corporation of Andhra Pradesh (LIDCAP), Handlooms 
and Textiles, Sericulture and Printing and Stationery in the Government of Andhra 
Pradesh, from 1981 to 1982.
Shri Palvai Govardhan Reddy  represented the State of Andhra Pradesh in this 
House from April, 2012 to June, 2014, and the State of Telangana from June, 2014 
till his sad demise. 
In the passing away of Shri Palvai Govardhan Reddy , the country has lost a 
distinguished parliamentarian and a dedicated social worker. 
Dr. C. Narayana Reddy  passed away on the 12th of June, 2017, at the age 
of 85 years.
Born in July, 1931, at Karimnagar District of Telangana, Dr. Reddy was educated 
at the Chaderghat College and the Osmania University. He was awarded honorary 
doctorates by several Universities.
A poet, Dr. Reddy  started his career as a Professor of Telugu at the Osmania 
University. He served as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Official Language 
Commission and the Andhra Pradesh State Cultural Council. He also served as the 
Vice-Chancellor of the Andhra Pradesh Open University from 1986 to 1989 and 
of the Telugu University from 1989 to 1992. He was the Advisor for Culture and 
Languages to the Government of Andhra Pradesh, from 1992 to 1995.
A prolific writer, Dr. Reddy has several volumes of poetry, lyrical plays, literary 
criticism, essays and several popular songs written for Telugu films to his credit. He 
was honoured with several awards and recognitions for his outstanding contribution 
to Telugu Literature, notable being the ' Padma Shri ' in 1977, Soviet Land Nehru 
Award in 1982, ' Jnanapith' Award in 1988 and the ' Padma Bhushan ' in 1992.

References by [17 July, 2017]   the Chair 5
Dr. C. Narayana Reddy  was a Nominated Member of this House from August, 
1997 to August, 2003.
In the passing away of Dr. C. Narayana Reddy,  the country has lost an eminent 
literateur and a distinguished parliamentarian. 
Shri U. K. Lakshmana Gowda  passed away on the 6th of July, 2017, at the 
age of 97 years. 
Born in December, 1919, at Chikmagalur District of Karnataka, Shri Gowda  
was educated at the Central College, Bengaluru.
A coffee planter and an agriculturist, Shri Gowda  was the founder Chairman 
of the Karnataka State Planters' Association and President of the United Planters' 
Association of Southern India.
Shri U. K. Lakshmana Gowda  represented the State of Karnataka in this House 
for two consecutive terms - from April, 1968 to April, 1974 and again from April, 
1974 to April, 1980. 
In the passing away of Shri U. K. Lakshmana Gowda , the country has lost 
an able parliamentarian.
We deeply mourn the passing away of Dr. Akhilesh Das Gupta, Shri Anil 
Madhav Dave, Shri P. N. Sukul, Dr. Dasari Narayana Rao, Shri Era Sezhiyan, 
Shri Palvai Govardhan Reddy, Dr. C. Narayana Reddy and Shri U. K. Lakshmana 
Gowda.
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved 
families our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.

REFERENCES BY THE CHAIR
Victims of torrential rains, landslides, floods and lightening strikes in  
North-Eastern States and several other parts of the country,  
terrorist attack in Anantnag District and bus accident  
in Ramban District of Jammu and Kashmir
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as you might be aware, several persons 
lost their lives and many others were injured, displaced and rendered homeless due 

6 References by [RAJYA SABHA] the Chair
to torrential rains, landslides, floods and lightening strikes in the States of Assam, 
Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu 
and Kashmir, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and some other 
parts of the country in the months of June and July, 2017. The incessant rains have 
also caused extensive damage to houses, property, infrastructure, crops and livestock.
The loss of precious lives and injury to people is indeed heartrending and 
unfortunate.
The House joins me in expressing heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the 
bereaved families and pray for the speedy recovery of the injured.
Hon. Members, it is with utmost grief and sorrow that I refer to the dastardly 
killing of seven Amarnath pilgrims and injury to 21 others in a terrorist attack in 
Anantnag district of Jammu and Kashmir, on the 10th of July, 2017. No words are 
strong enough to condemn this inhuman, barbaric and heinous act. The yatra, which 
symbolizes peace and harmony, is, however, continuing and the resilient attitude of 
the people in the face of such adversity is to be appreciated.
I am sure, the whole House will join me in condemning this cowardly and 
senseless act and in offering condolences to the bereaved families and also pray for 
speedy recovery of the injured. On this occasion, let us reiterate our firm resolve to 
fight terrorism with determination.
In another tragic incident, 16 Amarnath pilgrims reportedly lost their lives and 
around 30 others sustained injuries, when the bus in which they were travelling plunged 
into a gorge in Ramban district of Jammu and Kashmir, on the 16th of July, 2017.
The loss of precious lives and injury to people is indeed tragic and unfortunate.
The House joins me in expressing heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the 
bereaved families and pray for the speedy recovery of the injured.
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in these tragedies.
